skill.name: lark-event
skill.description: Stream Lark and Feishu events as NDJSON with lark-cli for messaging, tasks, meetings, minutes, and whiteboards. Use bounded consumers, schema-aware jq filters, ready markers, and graceful shutdown in agent-driven workflows.
skill.summary: Consume and filter real-time Lark events with reliable subprocess lifecycle guidance.
skill.author: larksuite

content.user_title: Stream Lark Events for Real-Time Workflows
content.value_statement: Real-time Lark workflows need reliable event streams, filtering, and clean shutdown behavior. This skill guides AI agents through bounded event consumption with lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Lists subscribable event keys and inspects their schema metadata with lark-cli.
Streams IM, Task, VC, Minutes, and Whiteboard events as NDJSON.
Filters and transforms individual events with schema-aware jq expressions.
Bounds consumers by event count or duration and interprets ready and exit markers.
Runs separate consumers for multiple event keys and supports graceful shutdown.
Explains required identities, scopes, and event-specific subscription behavior.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, configured credentials, required API scopes, and access to each target resource.
Each consumer handles exactly one event key, so multiple keys require separate processes.
Unbounded consumers require persistent stdin and may exit when stdin closes.
Some fields can be empty or absent because of scopes, source types, or enrichment failures.

use_cases.title: Build a responsive Lark bot
use_cases.description: Consume message and reaction events, then filter them for a bot response workflow.

use_cases.title: Automate task and meeting workflows
use_cases.description: Monitor task updates, meeting lifecycle events, and generated notes for downstream automation.

use_cases.title: Operate reliable event subscribers
use_cases.description: Use readiness markers, bounded runs, structured errors, and graceful termination in managed subprocesses.

prompt_templates.title: Discover available events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-cli to list available Lark event keys. Show the relevant schemas for [topic], but do not start a consumer.

prompt_templates.title: Sample one event
prompt_templates.prompt: Consume one [EventKey] event as [user or bot] with a 60-second timeout. Explain required scopes and summarize the output fields.

prompt_templates.title: Create a filtered stream
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bounded consumer for [EventKey] that selects [condition] and emits [fields]. Validate field paths against the event schema before writing jq.

prompt_templates.title: Design multi-event orchestration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-process subscription for [EventKey list]. Include ready-marker handling, independent bounds, structured errors, SIGTERM shutdown, deduplication, and sensitive-data controls.

output_examples.input: Sample one IM text message within 30 seconds.
output_examples.output: Prepared a bot consumer limited to one event and 30 seconds. The result includes sender, chat, message, and readable content fields.

output_examples.input: Watch edits for a specific whiteboard.
output_examples.output: Prepared a scoped whiteboard subscription using the required token. Each result identifies the whiteboard and its editor identifiers.

output_examples.input: Monitor meeting completion and generated notes.
output: Runs separate consumers because each process accepts one event key.
Waits for each ready marker before processing output.
Uses graceful termination so server-side subscriptions are cleaned up.

best_practices: Inspect each event schema before writing filters because root paths and decoded fields vary.
Use event count or timeout bounds during development, and preserve stderr ready and exit markers.
Use least-privilege identities, protect streamed content, and terminate with SIGTERM or stdin closure.
anti_patterns: Do not assume raw API payload shapes or apply fromjson to every content field.
Do not use kill -9 for subscriptions that require server-side cleanup.
Do not combine multiple event keys in one consumer or ignore nonzero exit codes.

faq.question: Which Lark events does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers IM, Task, video conference, Minutes, and Whiteboard event keys documented by lark-cli.

faq.question: What must be configured first?
faq.answer: Install lark-cli and configure an authorized user or bot with the scopes required by the selected event.

faq.question: Should I consume events as a user or bot?
faq.answer: Use the identity supported by the event schema and required resource access. Some events support only user authentication.

faq.question: Can one process consume several event keys?
faq.answer: No. Start one consumer per event key and coordinate their readiness, output, errors, and shutdown independently.

faq.question: How can I prevent a consumer from running indefinitely?
faq.answer: Set an event limit, a timeout, or both. Preserve stdin only when an unbounded subscriber is intentional.

faq.question: How should failures be handled?
faq.answer: Read structured errors from stderr, branch on error fields, and treat nonzero exit codes as failures.
